title: On the way
hook: the commute can be a pilgrimage
tomorrow: can wiping trays at 6 a.m. count as anything holy?

segments.voice: Yesterday, breakfast grace: thanks said before the first bite. The line was thanks first. Now, out the door.

The 5:40 bus, still dark. Hoods up, earbuds in, every face lit by the same small screen. Nobody on this ride would call it a journey, least of all the driver. It's the dead part of the day, between home and work. Mark tells about a road like that, the busy one out of Jericho, crowded with travelers. Jesus is on it, going up toward Jerusalem with his disciples and a big crowd. At the side of the road sits a blind man named Bartimaeus. He hears the crowd go by, and he starts to shout.
screen: `THE 5:40, STILL DARK.` → `THE ROAD OUT OF JERICHO.` → `A BLIND MAN STARTS TO SHOUT.`

segments.voice: The crowd tells him to be quiet. He shouts louder: son of David, have mercy on me. And here is the turn. Jesus stops. The whole procession, on its way up to the holy city, stands still for one man at the edge of the road. Jesus has him called over and asks a question that sounds almost too simple, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "What wilt thou that I should do to thee?" Bartimaeus asks to see. Mark ends the scene like this: "And immediately he saw, and followed him in the way." In the way. The same road, the same crowd, the same trip, with one more person on it who can now see. A pilgrimage, in Catholic practice, is a journey made as a prayer: the walking is part of it, not just the getting there. A commute can be that too. The route doesn't change. What changes is who you notice on it. Here's one to tell a friend tonight. The Catechism says the Jesus Prayer, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on us sinners, joins a hymn from Paul with the cry of the tax collector and of the blind men begging for light. A shout from the roadside became a prayer people still pray.
screen: `THE CROWD SAYS: BE QUIET.` · `JESUS STANDS STILL.` · `FOLLOWED HIM IN THE WAY.` · `THE ROUTE STAYS; THE NOTICING CHANGES.` · then, large: `A DAILY PILGRIMAGE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the route you take most days, stop by stop: the corner, the crossing, the person who's always at the same bus shelter. As each face comes up, give it one silent line, the Kyrie from Mass, Lord, have mercy, or simply a good wish. Keep going down the route until the bell.
On the way. The road between home and work, walked like a pilgrimage, the way Bartimaeus followed in the way.
Keep this one: a daily pilgrimage, the same road with your eyes up. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1625 COUNTS.` → `ORDINARY HOLINESS · 5 OF 80.` → `TOMORROW: CAN WIPING TRAYS AT 6 A.M. COUNT AS ANYTHING HOLY?`

howItsDone: Catholics make pilgrimages to shrines and holy places, praying along the road; some keep the same habit on an ordinary commute, praying for the people they pass.

fork.setup: on your bus, a man keeps asking people for change and the driver tells him to sit down. by Mark's road, what comes first?
options: look at him, actually see him; that's where the story starts.
look away; the driver has it handled.
change seats so the ride stays calm for everyone.
fork.reveal: the crowd told Bartimaeus to hush. Jesus stood still and called him over. noticing comes first; what you do next is yours to choose.

original.note: Greek: in the way, on the road. Mark's last words about Bartimaeus.

what it means: a daily pilgrimage: the same road, walked with your eyes up for the people on it.
what a scholar hears: Mark sets Bartimaeus on the road up to Jerusalem and ends with him following 'in the way' (Mark 10:52).

chat.says: got the panadería job!! first shift saturday: 5:40 bus in the dark. what do i do with that ride?
options: Make it a little pilgrimage. Notice who's on the bus and pray for them, like Jesus stopping on the road.
Sleep or study. A commute is dead time; the holy part starts once you get somewhere that matters.
Save prayer for Sunday. A real pilgrimage means a trip to a shrine, not a city bus at dawn.
chat.meaning: On Mark's road the whole crowd stopped for one man. A daily pilgrimage keeps the route and changes who you notice on it.

Bartimaeus.meaning: a blind man Jesus healed on the road out of Jericho

Jericho.meaning: an ancient town on the road up to Jerusalem

Kyrie.meaning: Greek for Lord: the Lord, have mercy prayed at Mass

Jesus Prayer.meaning: a short prayer asking Jesus for mercy, repeated slowly

Catechism.meaning: the Catholic Church's official summary of its teaching
